Colors

model.description:
This plugin localises all alias variables that refer to missing base variables (those located in external files or simply deleted)


Features

🚀 Instant Variable Localization — Automatically finds alias variables that lost their base/master links after copying and fixes them by creating local copies.

🔍 Live Preview Tree — Visualize the entire process before execution. See which variables will be newly created and which ones will be linked in a clean, hierarchical tree (alpha - there may be bugs here)

✨ Smart Collection Renaming — Option to automatically sync the name of your target collection with the original donor collection.

🌈 All Variable Types Supported — Works perfectly with Color, String, Boolean, and Number variables.


🎦 Video demonstration: https://youtu.be/f9Ofv7lB-Lk


Why is this a problem?!

Here's the thing... Figma doesn't care about links in alias variables, it doesn't transfer them to the new file, but leaves the links to the companion variables (base/master variables) in the old file. And this isn't what you expect when you copy variables :)


In simple words, what the plugin does:

  1. It looks for alias variables that have a reference to base variables that didn't make it to this file (either left in another file or simply missing)
  2. Creates copies of such variables in this file
  3. Rebinds the alias variable, changing the reference from the external master variable (base variable) to the newly created local one


Works for variables of all types:

  1. color,
  2. text,
  3. boolean,
  4. numeric

It should work with multiple mods, but I haven't tested this part.

🎦 Видео-демонстрация: https://youtu.be/f9Ofv7lB-Lk


Какую проблему решаем?

Figma не заботиться о связях алиас-переменной, она не переносит их в новый файл, а оставляет ссылки на переменные-спутники (базовые/мастер-переменные) в старом файле. А это вообще не то, чего ждёшь, когда копируешь переменные :)


Простыми словами, что делает плагин:

  1. Ищет переменные-алиасы, которые ссылаются на базовые переменные, не дошедшие до этого файла (либо оставшиеся в другом файле, либо пропавшие без вести)
  2. Создает копии таких переменных в этом файле
  3. Перевязывает алиас-переменную, меняя ссылку с внешней мастер-переменной (базовой переменной) на локальную


Работает для переменных всех типов:

  1. цветовые,
  2. текстовые,
  3. булевы,
  4. числовые

model.name: Variable Importer/Exporter
model.description:
The Variable Importer/Exporter plugin is used to create variables with ease and export them to a single source of truth in a JSON file!


Overview


The Variable Variable Importer/Exporter Plugin enables users to import and export variable collections within Figma. This functionality facilitates the definition and management of design tokens such as colors, spacings, and other attributes, ensuring consistency across different projects and among team members.


JSON Structure


The JSON file used by the plugin consists of an array of collections. Each collection can include multiple variables defined under different modes and types.


Collections


- name: The name of the collection (e.g., "Colors", "Spacing Tokens").

- modes: An array defining the modes applicable to the variables (e.g., "Default").

- variables: An object containing the variables. Each variable can have multiple shades or sizes, each defined with its type and value(s).


NOTE: You can only have one mode per collection with a free account. To have multiple modes, you need to have a paid account. I have not gotten a chance to test the feature with a free account yet.


Variable Types


Variables can be of the following types:


- color: For color values.

- number: For numeric values such as spacing.

- boolean: For true/false values.

- string: For textual values.


Values


Each variable type can contain values defined for each mode. Values can be direct (e.g., a hex code for colors) or referenced from another variable using the format `CollectionName:VariableName/PropertyName`.


## Example JSON


Here is an example JSON file for a color and spacing collection:


{
"collections": [
{
"name": "Colors",
"modes": ["Default"],
"variables": {
"Barn-Red": {
"50": {
"type": "color",
"values": { "Default": "#ffe6e6" }
},
"950": {
"type": "color",
"values": { "Default": "#3c0202" }
}
}
}
},
{
"name": "Spacing Tokens",
"modes": ["Default"],
"variables": {
"spacing": {
"0": { "type": "number", "values": { "Default": 0 } },
"768": { "type": "number", "values": { "Default": 768 } }
},
"padding": {
"sm": {
"type": "number",
"values": { "Default": "Spacing Tokens:spacing/4" }
}
}
}
}
]
}


Importing Variables


To import variables into Figma:


1. Prepare Your JSON File: Construct your JSON file according to the structure detailed above, including all necessary variable collections.

2. Use the Plugin: Open the plugin in Figma and use the import function to select and load your JSON file. The plugin will parse the JSON and create the corresponding variables in Figma.


Exporting Variables


To export variables from Figma:


1. Select Collection: Use the plugin interface to select the collection you wish to export.

2. Choose Color Format: Specify the color format for your export (Hex, RGB, HSL, with or without alpha).

3. Export: Initiate the export process, and the plugin will generate a JSON file representing the current state of the selected variables in the chosen color format. This file can be used in other projects or shared with team members.


Tips for Effective Usage


- Consistency is Key: Maintain consistent naming conventions for your collections and variables to simplify management and referencing.

- Leverage Referencing: Use references to link variables, enabling a scalable and easily updatable design system.

- Regular Exports: Regularly export your variable collections to keep backups and ensure that team members are working with the most current design tokens.

Varlint finds the values in your file that should be variables and are not, tells you which variable each one should be, and binds them.


YOUR IT REVIEW CAN CHECK THIS, NOT TAKE MY WORD

Varlint declares no network access, and Figma prints that on this page beside the last-updated date — so the person who approves plugins where you work can confirm it without contacting me. Your variables and your layers are already in your file; nothing about them leaves your machine, there is nothing to sign in to, and no usage is measured. There is nothing to fill in on a security questionnaire, and no service that can go down and take the plugin with it.


ALL 46 PLACES

Figma allows a variable in forty-six different places: sizes, spacing, corners, stroke weights, fill and stroke colour, every text property, effects, layout grids and component properties. Varlint looks at all of them. That number is not typed in by hand — a test reads Figma's own type definitions and fails if the two ever disagree.


IT SAYS WHICH VARIABLE

Finding a raw value is the easy half. If a variable in your file already holds that value, Varlint names it. If none does, it says so. It never offers to invent variables for you — your token set is yours.


DECISIONS, NOT ROWS

"Every padding of 16 should be spacing/md" is one decision that happens to touch thousands of layers. Varlint shows it as one row with the count on it, so a file's worth of work is a list you can actually read before you agree to it.


IT FOLLOWS YOUR FILE, NOT A RULEBOOK

Varlint reads how far your file has already got in each group — colour, spacing, corners, text — and only ticks the ones you are visibly already doing. A file that has never bound a width is not asked to start. When several variables hold the same value, the one your file already binds there wins. Nothing is guessed from variable names.


WHEN IT CAN'T, IT SAYS SO

Every binding is read back after it is written, and anything that did not take is listed with the reason: the layer is gone, the variable is gone, Figma will not allow it there. A binder that fails quietly is worse than one that fails.


FREE AND PAID

The audit is free, for ever: scan any page or the whole file, see the coverage figures, and see which variable every value should be. $5 once unlocks unlimited binding in every file you open. No subscription.

model.name: VarVar
model.description:
VarVar is a Figma plugin that allows you to export your Figma variables to JSON, JS, CSV, CSS, or Tailwind CSS formats, making it easier to integrate your design tokens into your development workflow. It can also import a previously exported JSON file back into a document, recreating collections, modes, variables, and linked variables.


Features

  1. Multiple Export Formats: JSON, JavaScript, CSV, CSS, and Tailwind CSS
  2. JSON Import§: Re-populate collections, modes, variables, and linked-variable references from a previously exported JSON file, with an optional "replace existing variables"
  3. Format-Specific Menu Commands: Direct access to each export format from the Figma menu
  4. Linked Variable Support: Properly handles linked variables across all formats†
  5. Scope-Aware Types: JSON, CSV, and JS exports map variable scopes (CORNER_RADIUS, FONT_WEIGHT, OPACITY, etc.) to DTCG $types instead of bare numbers
  6. Extended Collection Hierarchy Export (Enterprise, BETA)‡: All export formats detect Enterprise extended collections and preserve inherited vs. overridden values instead of flattening them. JSON additionally splits into a .zip of per-collection files when extended collections are present; CSS, CSV, and JS represent the inheritance inline in a single file.
  7. Legacy Format Toggle: JSON, CSV, and JS exports have a "legacy format (v2.x)" option to export in the pre-3.0 shape, for anyone whose tooling relies on it
  8. Preview & Copy: Preview exported data and easily copy to clipboard
  9. Download: Exported variables can be downloaded as files
  10. Row/Column Positioning: CSV option for spreadsheet formula-like linking


Linked Variable Handling

  1. JSON: Linked variables start with $.VARIABLE.PATH
  2. JavaScript: Linked variables are referenced directly like collection.mode.variable
  3. CSV: Linked variables start with =VARIABLE/PATH (with optional row/column positioning)
  4. CSS: Linked variables use CSS custom property syntax: --var-name: var(--VARIABLE)
  5. Tailwind CSS: Linked variables use CSS custom property syntax with Tailwind naming conventions


Notes:

† When dealing with linked variables that have multiple modes, the plugin will only link to the first occurrence (i.e., the first mode it finds).

‡ Enterprise fella? We'd love your feedback on this one, please open an issue with anything that looks off.

§ A leading `.` or `_` is Figma's own convention for marking a collection, variable, or group "private" (hidden from publishing). Import handles this correctly: linked-variable references are matched against your file's actual collection/mode names (so a `.` isn't confused with the JSON path separator), and any newly created collection/variable whose name starts with `.` or `_` gets `hiddenFromPublishing` set to match, so the privacy actually carries over rather than just looking private. Still review the import summary's warnings for anything it couldn't confidently match.


Usage

Design Mode

  1. Open your Figma file containing variables
  2. Run the VarVar plugin from the Plugins menu
  3. Choose your desired export format (JSON, JS, CSV or CSS)
  4. Click "Export Variables"
  5. Click "Download File". If `Preview output` is off, the exported file will be automatically downloaded


Dev Mode

  1. Open your Figma file containing variables
  2. Switch to Dev Mode
  3. Run the VarVar plugin from the Plugins menu
  4. Choose your desired export format (JSON, JS, CSV or CSS)
  5. Click "Export Variables"
  6. Click "Download File". If `Preview output` is off, the exported file will be automatically downloaded


Preview and Copy

  1. Toggle the "Preview output" switch to see the exported data within the plugin interface.
  2. Copy the results in one click!



Importing Variables (JSON)

  1. Open your Figma file
  2. Run the VarVar plugin from the Plugins menu
  3. Choose **Import…**
  4. Select one or more JSON files previously exported by VarVar
  5. Optionally turn on "Replace existing variables" — this deletes all existing local variable collections before importing, so you'll be asked to confirm first
  6. Click "Import Variables"


VarVar is open source, consider contributing. Code available on GitHub.

For bug reports, suggestions, or questions, please open an issue.

A Figma plugin for moving variables between collections while automatically updating all links in your designs.


Core Functionality

When you manually move a variable to a new collection in Figma, the connected layers usually lose their link (detach). Relink identifies these layers and reconnects them to the new variable IDs in the target collection.

  4. Optimization: Consolidated processing loops for better performance on heavy files.

Any automated modification of variable data carries risks. Before using the plugin:

  1. Create a Backup: Save a version in your Version History or duplicate the file.
  2. Use Branches: If you are on an Organization or Enterprise plan, we strongly recommend performing migrations in a branch. This allows you to verify the results before merging into the main file.

  2. Target: Choose the destination collection.

model.name: Remap & Swap Variables
model.description:
Two jobs, one click: repair broken variable links, and move your color

variables to another library — matched by name.


What it does

Remap — after a library is republished, bindings in your file can point at an outdated copy of a variable. The plugin finds those and repoints them to the current one. It matches on the variable's permanent key, so it never changes which variable you use — it only repairs the link. Always safe to run.


Swap — repoints your color variables to a target library collection you pick, matched by name. Anything with no matching name is left untouched and reported.


Great for

• Multi-brand / white-label theming — build a screen once, switch it to another

brand's colors, then flip between themes with Figma's native variable modes.

• Migrating a file from one variable library to another.

• Cleaning up stale variable bindings after a library update.


How to use

1. Enable your target library in Assets → Libraries (the book icon).

2. Open the plugin.

3. Manual tab: pick Target library → Target collection, then click Remap & swap.

It runs on the current page; a progress bar shows the run and a summary reports how many were remapped / swapped / had no name match.

Frames selected? A "Remap & Swap Selected" button appears to limit the run.

Save settings remembers your target for next time.

4. Auto watch tab: turn it on and pick a target. Every new frame you add or paste is remapped + swapped automatically as you work — minimize the plugin to a small bar that shows live progress. (Auto handles new frames; run Manual once to bring existing frames up to date.)

5. Logs tab: a history of every run that changed something, stored locally.


Good to know

• Works on color variables, matched by name — both libraries need to share variable names for the swap to connect.

• No-match names are left as-is and counted, so you can handle them yourself.

• Scoped to the current page (or your selection) — it won't touch other pages.

Have you ever had to search for variables by name and update them individually?

When working with Variables, you can turn multiple repetitive tasks into a single streamlined action.

model.description:
V2.1:

Variable References & Linked Aliases:

You can now use var(--other) inside a value to create a real Figma variable alias — not just a copied string. Cascading tokens like

--button--bg: var(--colors--primary);

stay linked: change the source variable and every variable pointing at it updates automatically. By default, the lookup happens inside the same collection you're feeding into.


Cross-Collection Linking with col(...):

To reference a variable that lives in a different collection, prefix the reference with col(CollectionName):

--button--bg: col(Colors), var(--primary);

Without col(...), the alias stays in the same collection. The order of declarations doesn't matter — aliases pointing at variables that are created later in the same batch are resolved in a second pass, and chains of alias-on-alias are supported.


Round-Trip-Safe Export:

When a Figma variable is aliased to a variable in another collection, the export now emits the col(CollectionName), var(--name) syntax automatically — so exporting and re-importing preserves every link, including across collections. A full round-trip through CSS is now lossless.


Reliable Clipboard Copy:

The "Copy to Clipboard" button on the export side now works reliably inside Figma's plugin iframe, with a built-in fallback that selects the output text if the system clipboard is blocked by the host environment.


Wider, Cleaner UI:

The plugin window is wider and uses a tidier two-column layout for collection and mode pickers, with taller input and output fields, a larger live preview that visualizes alias links with a "→ target" arrow, and clearer section grouping that surfaces detected modes and existing collections at a glance.

model.description:
What Isotop helps you do


  1. Generate a complete token system from a brand colour and a short brief
  2. Apply it to Figma as real variables, with semantic roles aliased to primitives
  3. Define and manage core color variables as a single source of truth
  4. Link and unlink design tokens to core variables, individually or in bulk
  5. Generate and evolve color palettes using reproducible recipes
  6. Work safely at scale with sandbox previews, Undo and Redo, and explicit syncing


Isotop is a professional tool for building and maintaining color and token systems in Figma, made for designers and teams working on real design systems rather than one-off color edits.


It does two jobs. It generates a token system for you, and it gives you the controls to keep the variables you already have structured and predictable, whether that is a small product or a large multi-collection system with deep dependencies.


___________________________________


Collider AI: generate the system


Collider is Isotop's AI system for token generation. Give it a brand colour and a short brief, and it builds the system in two layers: the primitives first, then the semantic roles that alias them.


Generation is guided. Collider works through the layer group by group and stops after each one, so you review colours before typography, and typography before spacing. Accept a group, edit it, regenerate it, or skip it. An accepted group can still be edited or regenerated later without disturbing the rest.


Every text-on-background pair the system implies is measured against its contrast floor while the layer is being built. When a pair falls short, the role is re-aimed at a primitive that clears it, never at a colour invented on the spot. Every role carries its value in each mode, so light and dark are one system, not two.


Nothing reaches your Figma file until you apply. Then the primitives land as variables, the semantic roles land as aliases pointing at them, type and shadow roles are compiled into named text and effect styles, and a documentation page is drawn from real Figma frames bound to the variables that were written. Each token carries its contract in the variable description, and the whole system exports to JSON.


Collider requires an Isotop account and runs on credits. Your prompt and design-system context are sent to our AI provider to generate suggestions; your account identifier and email are not.


___________________________________

Variable Chain Visualiser

See how your variables really connect.


What it does


Figma variables often point to other variables instead of holding a value on their own. A button color might point to a brand color, which points to a base color, which finally points to a hex code. This is called aliasing, and it is how most design systems are built today.


The problem is that these chains are invisible in Figma's own panel. As a file grows past a few dozen variables, nobody can see the full picture anymore. Broken links, unused variables, and confusing chains build up quietly, and nobody notices until something breaks on screen.


Alias Chain Visualizer scans your whole file in one pass and lays out every chain so you can actually see it.


Features


See the full picture

Every variable in your file, shown in one view. Primitive values, semantic tokens, and component variables, laid out side by side so you can trace how they connect.


Trace any chain

Click on any variable to follow its full path, from the raw value all the way up to where it is used.


Find what is broken

The plugin checks for five common problems in your file:


Broken links, where a variable points to something that no longer exists

Loops, where a chain circles back on itself

Unused variables, that nothing else in the file references

Chains that go too deep, making them hard to follow or maintain

Values that stop working in certain modes


Check every mode

Switch between Light, Dark, or any other mode your file uses, and see if a variable still resolves the way it should in each one.


See what depends on it

Click into any variable to see every component that uses it. Know exactly what you would affect before you make a change.


Read-only, always

The plugin only looks at your file. It never edits, renames, or deletes anything. You stay fully in control of every change.


Why it helps


Design systems get harder to trust as they grow. A small typo or a missed link can sit inside a chain for months before anyone notices it in the actual design. This plugin gives you a way to check your file on your own terms, instead of finding problems by accident later.


It also makes onboarding easier. New team members can open the plugin and see how the whole token system fits together, instead of clicking through dozens of variables one at a time.


Who it is for


Designers who maintain a variable library and want to understand what they are changing before they change it

Design system leads who run periodic checks to keep the file healthy

Teams handing off a design system to someone new, who need a fast way to explain how it works


How it works


Open the plugin, run a scan, and browse the results. There is no setup, no configuration, and nothing to connect. It works entirely inside the file you already have open.

model.description:
Companion V3.0 is here!

In this release, we're going beyond plugins to help you streamline your design workflow.


We're introducing "Resources", a new tab dedicated to display a curated list of design resources, from websites, icon libraries, color tools, mockups and much more.


―――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――


Advanced Color Finder

  1. A powerful tool that allows you to search for colors across your files.
  2. Ultra-fast search algorithm with advanced labeling
  3. Colors are grouped by type (variable or style) and by source (Remote or local libraries)
  4. Ability to search by variable name, color hex and by layer name


Text Extractor

  1. Extract, search and export text content from selected items
  2. Export to Excel and CSV formats


Style Guide Generator

  1. Transform your color collections into a beautiful style guide
  2. Choose one or more color formats to display (HEX, RGB, HSL)
  3. Support for cross-collections linked variables


Contrast Checker

  1. Check for AA and AAA level compliance
  2. Interactive and instant results when adjusting colors
  3. Live preview and swap foreground and background colors
  4. Get results for for text (Small / Large) and graphics elements


Tints & Shades Generator

  1. Interactive generator with live colors preview
  2. Ability to customize the number of generated colors
  3. Built-in contrast checker
  4. Preview generated colors on canvas
  5. Save generated colors to variables


Color Converter

  1. Convert any given color to popular color formats
  2. Currently supports HEX, RGB, HSL, CMYK, HSV, OKLCH and LAB
  3. Select and copy results


Sort Layers

A set of different ways to sort your layers within Figma.

  1. Alphabetical sorting (A-Z or Z-A)
  2. Sort by X or Y position on the canvas
  3. Sort by layer type (Frame, text, group, section, etc…)
  4. Reverse current sorting
  5. Magically sort everything based on names and positions


Distribute Layers

A powered up version of Figma’s built-in distribute feature.

  1. Distribute selected layers horizontally or vertically
  2. Set a desired value for the space between layers
  3. Ability to align layers from top (in horizontal mode) or left (in vertical mode)


Display As Grid

  1. Quickly rearrange selected layers in a grid layout with improved alignment and sorting features
  2. Ability to choose the number of columns along with vertical and horizontal gaps
  3. Ability to align columns vertically or not
  4. Extra sorting capabilities for better organization


Scale Layers

  1. Scale one or more layers
  2. Choose a specific width, height or percentage
  3. Specify scaling direction


Hidden Layers

Simple yet powerful tool to bulk manage hidden layers. It allows you to

  1. Hide selected layers
  2. Show all hidden layers within a page or within a selection
  3. Select all hidden layers within a page or within a selection
  4. Delete all hidden layers within a page or within a selection


Locked Layers

Simple yet powerful tool to bulk manage locked layers. It allows you to

  1. Lock or unlock selected layers
  2. Lock or unlock all layers on a page


Remove Numbers

Get rid of all those annoying numbers that Figma automatically generates. A single click gets the job done


Ungroup Single Layers Group

Optimize your files by ungrouping single layers group or deleting empty groups


Start at 0, 0

It’s just the cherry on top. A file is never tidy unless you start at 0, 0 — and for that, we got you covered


Case Converter

Easily convert selected layers names to Sentence case, upper case, lower case, camel case and more...


Country Flags

Insert SVG flags directly into your canvas, in both rectangular and square formats


Fix Detached Instances

  1. Preview and fix all detached instances within your files.
  2. Find all detached instances across pages
  3. Preview of the original component versus the detached instance
  4. Link instance to original component
  5. Maintain all manual overrides


Find and Reset Instance Overrides

  1. Scan your pages for instance overrides
  2. Bulk select by override type (ex. reset all overriden strokes)
  3. Basic and advanced mode for better control


Components Sitemap Generator

  1. Generate a full sitemap of components in your file with number of variants, component description and documentation link


Change Page Background

  1. Easily change the current page background
  2. Choose from available presets or set a custom color
  3. Bulk apply to all pages in your file


Grid Calculator

  1. Generate custom grids or use existing templates
  2. Live preview of the grid
  3. Add the grid to your file with a click


Clear Variable Modes

  1. Clear all variable modes (ex: light / dark mode) applied to elements on the current or all pages or across all pages in the file


Count Frames

  1. Count frames on current page or across the whole file
  2. Specify frame width, height, visibility (optional)


Magic Search

Unique and ultra-fast way to find any layer within your file. The algorithm has been thoroughly optimized for speed, especially for large files.


How it works:

  1. Start by selecting the layer type (Frame, text, rectangle, etc.) or choose “All Layers” to search everything
  2. Choose one or more properties to search for (Fill color, width, font, etc.)
  3. Hit the search button and voilà. Results are there.
  4. Browse the list of matching search results, with ability to filter by layer name.
  5. Click on a result to view it on the canvas or click “Select All” to bulk select all matching results


Here are some example scenarios:

  1. [Simple] ― Find all text layers with the font “Inter” and font weight “Semi Bold”
  2. [Simple] ― Find all rectangles with a corner radius of 16 and corner smoothing of 60%
  3. [Medium] ― Find all instances of a component named “Button” that are hidden and have been detached
  4. [Advanced] ― Find all instances of an external library component named “Input” that are marked as ready for dev and whose top left corner radius is less than or equal to 20px


In short, the possibilities are endless


MagiConnect

MagiConnect is a simple and easy to use tool that allows you to draw connectors between your frames. Some key features include:

  1. Auto-draw mode: When enabled, it allows you to quickly draw connectors between any two elements you select on the canvas. The direction of the connector arrow is based on the selection order
  2. Manual mode was designed to give you more flexibility in accessing nested layers before drawing a connector. It’s slower for sure, but gives you more control
  3. You can customize the connector by adjusting the color, opacity, stroke width, radius and stroke style

model.name: eval()
model.description:
Calculators are dead. 💀 Do math and run code right on the canvas inside Figma files! ✨ Select a text layer, frame or group and run the plugin, the result of the last line expression will be printed on canvas below the expression.


Send the plugin link to your friends: https://figma.fun/eval 🔗


Copy examples below, paste them as separate text objects in your file and run the plugin.


Evaluate an expression (RIP calculators 💀)

75 + 69 * 5


Generate a random number [0-100]

Math.round(Math.random() * 100)


Count all layers in the file (don't run in large files!)

figma.root.findAll(n => true).length


Tips:

  1. You can select multiple objects to run at once but each layer will run in a separate function and the variables won't be shared across.
  2. The code is written in JavaScript.
  3. You can access all Figma API methods within the code.
  4. Write code in text blocks, code blocks, stickies and shapes with text (last three only in FigJam).
  5. Select groups or frames to run all the code inside. Except for output nodes, which would be updated with the new calculation result.
  6. If you want to see output, the last line in the text box should be an expression that returns a value (examples: 5 + 5, myfunc(), x) and not a statement (such as const p = 4).
  7. Add // at the beginning of the text node so it's treated as a comment and doesn't produce a result.
  8. Add = at the end of the expression so the result is printed in the same text, for example: 5 + 5 = would be turned into 5 + 5 = 10.
  9. The node with code can be hidden or transparent and the result would be still printed visible. This is useful if you want to not clutter the file with code.
  10. If your code throws an error, it will be printed in red.
  11. The plugin works similar to notebooks in Python or other interpreted languages.


Tips, questions and feedback are welcome in the comments!

model.name: DesignCheck
model.description:
DesignCheck 是一款面向 Figma 设计团队的设计规范校验插件。选中任意图层，自动提取颜色、圆角、间距、字体以及特效（Effects）等设计参数，智能匹配本地变量和引入的组件库，支持一键批量绑定——让你的设计稿始终与设计系统保持一致。


  1. 核心功能


  1. 五维参数提取：自动识别选中图层的颜色（含 8 位色值+不透明度）、圆角半径、间距、字体参数，以及特效集合。
  2. 组件库匹配：加载团队 UI Kits 后，自动匹配引入的组件库中的变量和文本样式（Text Style），覆盖本地 + 库双通道。
  3. 远程抓取团队库：除已引入的组件库外，还可填入 Figma personal access token，直接抓取任意库源文件的颜色 / 文本 / 特效样式。
  4. 一键绑定变量：逐项或一键批量将图层属性绑定到匹配的变量，支持六类绑定——颜色填充（fills）、圆角（cornerRadius）、间距（itemSpacing）、字号（fontSize）、文本样式（Text Style），以及整组特效（Effect Style / EFFECT 变量）。
  5. 已绑定状态可视化：已绑定的属性以圆点预览实际颜色值（颜色/字体 tab），圆角/间距 tab 支持隐藏 0px 过滤，一目了然。
  6. 图层快速定位：点击列表中的图层名即可在 Figma 中聚焦到对应图层。
  7. 中英双语界面：内置语言切换按钮，中文 / English 一键切换，选择自动记忆，下次打开沿用。并支持一键最小化按钮收起插件面板。
  8. 变量模式切换（Variable Mode）：对应 Figma 外观（Appearance）中的「应用变量模式」。选中图层后，插件在顶部显示「变量模式」条，按变量集合逐个列出下拉框；切换后，列表中变量的有效值会按当前生效模式实时重写。仅当文档存在含 ≥2 个模式的变量集合、且选区用到了该集合变量时才出现，避免无意义的切换。


  1. 使用方式


  1. 打开 DesignCheck 插件。
  2. 在 Figma 中选中一个或多个图层。
  3. 填入库源文件链接与 Figma personal access token，点「抓取」拉取该库全部样式，再点「加载外部组件」匹配。已引入的库无需 token，直接加载即可。
  4. 查看五个 Tab：**颜色 / 字体 / 圆角 / 间距 / 特效**，每个属性显示当前值及是否匹配到变量。
  5. 变量模式：若文档含多模式变量集合，顶部「变量模式」条会按集合列出下拉框。选择一个模式即可对当前选区应用外观模式切换（如 Light / Dark），列表中的变量有效值会实时按生效模式重写。
  6. 点击「绑定」按钮逐项绑定，或使用「一键绑定」批量完成所有未绑定项。
  7. 需要暂时收起面板时，点击右上角「─」最小化按钮，再次点击即可还原。


  1. 适用场景


- 设计走查：检查设计稿是否使用了设计系统中的正确变量。

- 变量迁移：从硬编码样式迁移到设计变量体系。

- 团队协作：确保团队成员统一使用引入的组件库变量，保持设计一致性。

- UI Kit 接入：快速将设计稿对接团队发布的 UI Kit 组件变量库。

-外观 / 主题切换：对选定图层快速应用变量集合的模式（如明暗主题 Light / Dark），无需逐层手动改模式。


  1. 技术规格


- 支持 Figma 变量、文本样式与特效样式

- 兼容本地变量集合与引入的组件库

- 可选远程抓取：通过用户自填的 Figma personal access token 调用官方 读取库样式，token 仅存于本地、不发往任何第三方。

-变量模式：支持对选区显式应用 / 清除变量集合模式。

---


  1. Description (English)


DesignCheck is a Figma plugin that validates your design specs across five dimensions—color, typography, corner radius, spacing, and effects—and binds them to your variable library with one click. Select any layer to instantly see its design tokens matched against local variables and imported component libraries, then batch-bind everything at once to keep your designs always in sync with your design system.


  1. Features
  2. Extracts 5 types of design parameters: color (8-digit hex + opacity), corner radius, spacing, typography, and effects collections (drop shadow / inner shadow / blur / noise / texture / glass / shader, etc.).
  3. Matches variables from both local collections and imported component libraries (UI Kits), including Text Styles and Effect Styles.
  4. Optional remote library fetch: paste a Figma personal access token to pull styles (color / text / effect) from any library file.
  5. One-click batch binding for fills, corner radius, spacing, font size, Text Styles, and whole Effect Styles / EFFECT variables.
  6. Visual bound-state indicators with color preview dots; 0px filtering for radius/spacing; whole-group status for effects.
  7. Click layer names to focus in the Figma canvas.
  8. Bilingual UI: switch between Chinese and English via the language button; preference is saved for next launch,and a one-click minimize button.
  9. Variable Mode switching: maps to Figma's "Apply variable mode" in Appearance. With a layer selected, a "Variable modes" bar shows a per-collection dropdown; Effective variable values in the list rewrite live to the active mode. The bar only appears when the document has a variable collection with ≥2 modes that the selection actually uses.


  1. How to Use
  2. Open the DesignCheck plugin.
  3. Select layer(s) in Figma.
  4. (Optional) To match a library NOT yet linked to the current document: paste the library file link and your Figma personal access token, click "Fetch" to pull its styles, then "Load External Components" to match. Already-linked libraries load directly without a token.
  5. Browse the Colors / Font / Radius / Spacing / Effects tabs.
  6. (Optional) Variable modes: if the document contains multi-mode variable collections, a "Variable modes" bar lists a dropdown per collection. Pick a mode to apply appearance-mode switching (e.g., Light / Dark) to the current selection; the effective variable values update live.
  7. Click individual "Bind" buttons or use "Bind All" to bind everything at once.
  8. Click the "─" minimize button in the top-right to collapse the panel, and click again to restore.

model.name: Pigment
model.description:
Pigment reads a design token JSON file and creates Figma Color Variables

for you, no manual setup, no copy-pasting hex codes one by one.


It builds two variable collections automatically:


Primitives - your raw color values (e.g. gray/10, purple/500)

Semantics - usage-based aliases that reference your primitives

(e.g. brand/primary → purple/500, neutral/bg → gray/10)


Opacity (Alpha) Variants


You can generate opacity variants for any color token. Choose which

tokens need alpha stops and at what percentages, Pigment creates them

in the Primitives collection.


Pick from four presets:


  1. Light (10, 20, 30) - for subtle overlays, hover states, and disabled tints. Generates 3 variables per token.


  1. Standard (10, 20, 50, 80) - the default. Covers most design system needs across transparent, mid, and heavy opacity. Generates 4 variables per token.


  1. Dense (5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 80, 90) - full coverage for tokens used heavily in theming, like your primary brand color or key surface color. Generates 7 variables per token.


  1. Custom - pick any combination from 11 available stops (5 through 95). For edge cases and specific design decisions.


What format does it accept?

model.description:
Relay moves your work between the design board and Figma Make, in both directions.


Prompting Make to recreate a design can take hours of back and forth, and Make's "Copy design" gives you a flat snapshot with no real structure. Relay fixes both.


DESIGN → MAKE

Select your frames, paste your file link, and Relay writes numbered prompts Make understands:

- Exact colours, type styles, variables, spacing and auto layout

- Components with their variants and properties

- Every prototype interaction, with timing and easing

- The right start screen, picked from your prototype

- Optional phone, tablet and desktop versions

Copy step 1, paste it into Make, then paste each next step into the chat. Plain-English steps guide you all the way.


MAKE → DESIGN

Download your project from Make's Code tab and upload the .zip. Relay rebuilds it as real, editable Figma layers:

- Every screen the app can show, not just the one on screen

- Real auto layout with fill, hug and fixed sizing, plus constraints

- Repeated parts as components with variants and text properties

- Theme colours as variables, your fonts, Lucide icons and images

- Prototype links with the app's own timing, dialogs and sheets as overlays, and hover states


PRIVATE BY DESIGN

Relay runs entirely on your computer. It has no network access, uses no AI and never uploads your designs or code.


FREE AND PRO

Free: 2 frames per run to Make, 1 screen at a time from Make, at full quality.

Pro: unlimited frames and screens, whole prototype flows, prototype interactions, colour variables, extra screen sizes and screen picking. Try Pro free for 7 days.


GOOD TO KNOW

Relay builds each screen's resting state: animations that loop, scroll effects and live data from the internet aren't included. If a Make project doesn't come through correctly, send the zip through the support link and it'll be fixed for everyone.


From the maker of Choreo, prompt-driven motion for Figma.
